name: Error Prevention
description: It is better to stop an error from being possible, or make it hard, than to rely on a good error message afterward. Good design removes traps before recovery is needed.
design_relevance_note: Applies to destructive confirmations, sensible defaults, constraints, input masks, inline validation, irreversible actions, and progressive disclosure of risky choices.
myth_risk_note: Updated 2026-09-07: myth risk is low because, unlike several other entries in this corpus's Popular-but-Unverified pool, the core claim behind this heuristic (system design can prevent real errors) now has genuine, if domain-narrow, empirical support rather than none at all.
prevalence_note: A baseline heuristic across forms, transactions, admin tools, and safety-critical flows; commonly invoked in both product design and design-system reviews.

findings.description: Across two pediatric hospitals over 6 months, pharmacist review of physician medication orders caught errant orders (most commonly incorrect dosage) before they reached patients, meaningfully reducing potential harm -- a human-oversight-layer demonstration of error prevention, complementing the system/interface-design demonstrations from src-bates-1999 and src-overhage-1997.
findings.effect_size: 281 and 198 errant orders detected across the two hospitals (4.9 and 4.5 per 1,000 medication orders respectively); no single pooled effect size reported
findings.source_title: Medication Error Prevention by Clinical Pharmacists in Two Children's Hospitals

findings.description: In a randomized trial, physicians who received automated, guideline-based "corollary order" reminders while writing orders complied with the suggested follow-up test/treatment more than twice as often as control physicians who received no reminder -- a real-time system-design intervention directly preventing errors of omission.
findings.effect_size: 46.3% compliance with suggested corollary orders (intervention) vs. 21.9% (control), P<.0001
findings.source_title: A Randomized Trial of "Corollary Orders" to Prevent Errors of Omission
findings.source_venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association

findings.description: Introducing computerized physician order entry (CPOE) with decision-support features (drug-allergy and drug-drug-interaction warnings) reduced non-missed-dose medication errors by 81% and serious (injury-potential) errors by 86% across a 4-period prospective time-series study in real hospital units -- a large, precisely measured demonstration that system-design constraints prevent real errors, though scoped to a medical-IT context rather than Nielsen's general interface heuristic.
findings.effect_size: 81% reduction in non-missed-dose medication errors (142 to 26.6 per 1,000 patient-days, P<.0001); 86% reduction in serious errors (P=.0003)
findings.source_title: The Impact of Computerized Physician Order Entry on Medication Error Prevention
findings.source_venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association

applications.title: 2018 Hawaii false ballistic-missile alert -- a menu-design error-prevention failure
applications.description: On January 13, 2018, a Hawaii Emergency Management Agency operator selected a live 'PACOM (CDW) - STATE ONLY' missile-alert option instead of the adjacent, similarly-labeled drill option on a cluttered, poorly differentiated alert-type menu, sending a real 'BALLISTIC MISSILE THREAT INBOUND' warning to residents' phones statewide. The retraction took 38 minutes, partly because the system had no built-in undo or retraction-message type.
applications.ethical_note: This is a structural error-prevention failure in public-safety software, not a persuasion or dark-pattern case -- there is no user-beneficial/manipulative axis to weigh, since no party is trying to influence behavior through psychological framing. It is included specifically because it is one of the most consequential, well-documented real-world illustrations of what happens when a system's own design causes an operator slip, which is exactly the failure mode error prevention as a heuristic exists to guard against.
